si_4_title.answer: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative models were trained using Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping (sinarcsinsh function) implemented in python 3.8 and PCNtoolkit package (version 0.20). Models were pretrained on data from 58,835 individuals.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: normative models were trained using Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping using sinarcsinsh function [46]. ... Models were both trained and applied to our data using python 3.8 and PCNtoolkit package (version 0.20).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional cortical thickness and surface area (summarized using the Destrieux atlas) and subcortical volumes (segmented using a probabilistic atlas) were used as dependent variables.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: lifetime normative trajectories of cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volumes. ... Cortical thickness and area was summarized using the Destrieux atlas parcellation scheme [43]. Subcortical volume segmentation was based on a probabilistic atlas with priors for 31 brain structures [44, 45].

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and scanner were used as the independent variables in the normative models. Intracranial volume (ICV) was used as a covariate in subsequent statistical analyses (GLMs) for area and volume contrasts, but not in the primary normative models.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: the independent variables were age and scanner. ... Additionally, for analyses contrasting volumes and areas, we included intracranial volume (ICV).
